question: On 19 February2024, the European Commission and Rwanda signed a Memorandum of Understanding to work together to set up sustainable raw material value chains. At the same time, Rwanda is actively involved in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, an area bordering Rwanda very rich in minerals. It does so through its support to the violent rebel group M23.

On 7 July 2023, Josep Borrell, Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, condemned Rwanda’s military presence in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda’s support to M23. 1.
Can it be ensured that no sustainable value chains or other projects are established under the MoU in the region of Congo occupied by M23?
To what extent did the Commission take account of the underlying connections between Rwanda and the armed group M23 prior to the conclusion of this Memorandum?

What are the specific measures that the Commission will take to ensure that cooperation with Rwanda in establishing sustainable raw materials value chains does not contribute to the financing or strengthening of armed groups such as M23 operating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo?
answer: The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed with Rwanda formalises the common intention to support the sustainable and responsible sourcing, production and processing of raw materials. Mutually beneficial partnerships on raw materials with different countries in the region are one of the intended tools to implement the renewed EU Great Lakes Strategy (1).

They include cooperation on sustainability and governance standards, including with regard to the impacts of extractive and processing activities on human rights and conflicts. Consequently, the MoU should help increase traceability and transparency.

The EU has strongly urged Rwanda to immediately withdraw all its military personnel from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as well as to terminate all support to and cooperation with the March 23 Movement (M23), while also strongly urging the DRC and all regional players to terminate all support to and cooperation with armed groups including the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) (2).

The EU has also been improving mineral resources management and reducing its impact on conflict through the programme ‘Peace and Security for Stability in the Great Lakes region’ (3), which supports the revision and implementation of the Regional Certification Mechanism. The MoU also supports Rwanda’s engagement with the Extractive Industry Transparency Initiative (4).

Renewed EU Great Lakes Strategy, 20 February 2023: https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-6631-2023-INIT/en/pdf EU Statement of 4 March 2024: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2024/03/04/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-drc-statement-by-thehigh-representative-on-behalf-of-the-eu-on-the-escalation-of-hostilities-in-the-eastern-part-of-the-country/ Details of this programme are available at this link: https://mirego.bi/applications/views/UE.php
